title: A Mechanism for the Rényi Hierarchy of Decoherence-Induced Phase Transitions
authors: Zhou Yang, Yuri D. Lensky, Chao-Ming Jian
abstract: Decoherence-induced phase transitions (DIPTs) are associated with singular changes in a quantum system's entanglement structure as the decoherence strength varies. In many cases, their critical strengths depend monotonically on the Rényi index of the entanglement diagnostic, forming a Rényi hierarchy. We identify a general mechanism for this hierarchy based on correlation inequalities in replicated statistical models that describe these DIPTs. We demonstrate it in $\mathbb{Z}_2$ topological stabilizer codes subject to independent phase-flip decoherence on each qubit and in a decohered rotor model with strong $\text{U}(1)$ symmetry. When the relevant correlations diagnose the DIPTs, these inequalities imply that the critical decoherence strength is nondecreasing with integer Rényi index $R\geq2$. We show that this mechanism also applies to a class of models with correlated decoherence.
summary: This theoretical paper establishes a general mechanism for the Rényi hierarchy of Decoherence-Induced Phase Transitions (DIPTs) by analyzing correlation inequalities in replicated statistical models. Using models like topological codes and rotor systems, the authors prove that the critical decoherence strength increases monotonically with the Rényi index $R$ for $R \ge 2$. This provides a deep mathematical understanding of how entanglement diagnostics reveal the structure of quantum phase boundaries under noise.
main_problem: The paper aims to identify a general, underlying mechanism responsible for the Rényi hierarchy observed in Decoherence-Induced Phase Transitions (DIPTs). This hierarchy dictates that the critical decoherence strength increases monotonically with the Rényi index $R$ for $R \ge 2$.
main_result: A general mechanism is established using correlation inequalities within replicated statistical models, proving that the critical decoherence strength $p_c(R)$ is non-decreasing with $R$ for $R \ge 2$ in various models.

model_or_system: The study applies to $Z_2$ topological stabilizer codes subjected to phase-flip decoherence, and a decohered rotor model exhibiting strong U(1) symmetry. The physics is analyzed via replicated partition functions $Z_R$.

why_interesting: This work provides a powerful, general mathematical tool—the correlation inequality approach—to predict and understand the structure of quantum phase transitions driven by environmental coupling, which is crucial for understanding quantum error correction and open quantum systems.
